subject: FY23 School Budget Public Hearing
overview: The committee held a statutory public hearing on the $69 million FY23 budget, focusing on strategies to reconcile a $4 million gap between requested funds and the mayor's proposed appropriation. The body discussed the use of one-time COVID-19 relief funds and revolving accounts to maintain level services despite projected shortfalls.

items.title: FY23 Budget Presentation and Reconciliation
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent of Finance David Murphy presented a budget of approximately $69 million, which requires bridging a $4 million gap from the initial $72.5 million request through position eliminations and grant funding. The plan includes a 2% cost of living increase and shifts various expenses to external or revolving funds to preserve core operations.

items.title: ESSER and ARPA Funding Strategy
items.summary: The administration detailed the allocation of $6.2 million in remaining ESSER funds over the next two fiscal years to support English learner programs, social-emotional learning, and COVID-19 mitigation. Mayor Lungo-Koehn noted that city ARPA funds were also utilized for school infrastructure and testing to preserve school-specific relief grants.

items.title: Public Comment and Override Debate
items.summary: A resident requested a Proposition 2 1/2 override to provide higher teacher raises and address long-term funding gaps. Mayor Lungo-Koehn and Member Ruseau debated the merits of an override versus living within current means and growing the commercial tax base.

items.title: School Committee Goals and Student Representation
items.summary: Approved a motion to hold a dedicated goals-setting meeting in September to establish annual priorities and accountability measures. The committee also discussed improving the consistency of student representation at future meetings.
